subject: From XeTeX code to HTML through knitr?

messages.author: dd07e88083ca7a5d
messages.subject: From XeTeX code to HTML through knitr?
parts:
Hello everyone,

my professor and I have written a basic R tutorial (for linguistics) in Xetex (that Tex distribution seemed to work best for our purposes).
Considering that knitr can produce HTML as well, my question is whether there is a way to use knitr for the conversion.
I know that we could simply manually "convert" the Xetex code into RMarkdown, would you recommend doing that? Our Tex document contains a cover page, a number of images, a standard bibliography (from a .bib file, using \bibliography{}), simple tables, bits of R code, but no mathematical formulas, for example.

(You can view the pdf here: http://www.academia.edu/6867575/R_Basics_for_Linguistic_Typology_1_First_steps)

I very much appreciate your advice.

Markus

messages.author: dd07e88083ca7a5d
messages.subject: Re: From XeTeX code to HTML through knitr?
parts: I should add that the general idea is to make the document available online, ideally as an HTML document on the university website.

messages.author: 8502567f9dbc7c7e
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] From XeTeX code to HTML through knitr?
parts:
When you say "convert" the tool that comes to my mind is pandoc. Knitr is a meta-tool for "knit-ing" results from R (or other analysis languages) into text documents, of which Markdown and LaTeX are two possible variants. That is, you write in your choice of a pairing of analysis language and text format, and get out just the text format. Knitr does not make it any easier to spit out different text formats from the same source.

If the paper is in your mind done, pandoc is probably more appropriate. If you want to change how you construct your document for further development, knitr is a good choice for constructing your source documents if you are bringing in a lot of R output.

However, whether you include pandoc in your tool chain or not, usually some customization of the source file is necessary depending on the output format, so I have not found success generating multiple good-looking output formats from the same source and have to settle for some hand customization of the alternate formats output formats.
